Subject: Forensics retention and SIG evidence request

Hi Priya,

We're wrapping up our SIG/CAIQ and need a short, customer-facing summary of Redwood's tenant log retention for forensic scopes, plus any evidence you can provide to validate retention/deletion behavior for our account (Greenline). Specifically: 

- Can you confirm default retention windows for transaction logs, inference debug traces, and KV cache snapshots for hosted customers?
- If a customer requests a temporary hold for forensics (legal incident), what is the workflow and who are the data custodians?
- Are there any documented exceptions or carve-outs you allow for tenant-level retention different from platform defaults? If yes, what approvals are required?

We also attached a short checklist for SIG evidence (we'll email it separately). Ideally we'd like a concise statement we can keep for auditors and any supporting artifacts (sample TTL matrix, proof-of-delete process, and contact for on-call custodian).

Thanks — appreciate a response within 48 hours if possible.

Karen Li
Security Program Manager
Greenline Health
karen.li@greenlinehealth.com

[attachment: greenline_sig_evidence_checklist.pdf]

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Karen Li <karen.li@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Forensics retention and SIG evidence request

Hi Karen — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Jordan (security ops) and Marissa (Customer Success / evidence pack) so we can pull a short attestation and supporting artifacts.

Quick answers up front:
- Platform defaults: transaction logs = 90 days; inference debug traces (session-level) = 30 days; KV cache snapshots are ephemeral (24–72 hours) unless you opt into extended retention (see options below).
- Temporary hold: we can apply a tenant-specific forensics hold; the workflow is: customer request -> CS intake -> Legal approval (if required) -> Security Ops apply hold (snapshots + extended log retention) -> evidence export. Custodians: Security Ops on-call (primary: Jordan) and the assigned TAM (Marissa).
- Exceptions: We support temporary extension or carve-outs for customers with signed agreement addenda (retainer or SLA addendum). Those require Legal sign-off + approval from Head of Security.

We'll prepare: a one-page customer attestation, the TTL matrix CSV, and a short runbook describing the hold workflow + custodian contacts. Expect a first pass by EOD Monday.

Warmly,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.ai

Priya / Marissa — draft attestation (customer-facing) attached below, plus the TTL matrix (redwood_log_ttl_matrix.csv). Key points included: 

- Default retention: transaction logs (90d), inference session traces (30d), KV cache snapshots (24–72h).
- Forensics hold: we capture immutability checkpoint + exportable event stream; Security Ops generates a signed chain-of-custody PDF and a proof-of-delete report when hold is released.
- Exceptions: tenant-specific extensions only via signed addendum (Legal) + Security Ops authorization.

I've uploaded redacted examples to the Drive folder. Draft attestation excerpt below — please review for legal tone: 

"Redwood Inference attests that, absent a customer-specific written addendum, tenant-level transaction logs are retained for 90 days, inference session traces for 30 days, and ephemeral KV caches for up to 72 hours. Upon customer request for forensic preservation, Redwood will apply a tenant-scoped hold and generate exportable artifacts (immutable checkpoint + signed chain-of-custody). Temporary retention extensions are supported only under a signed addendum and with Security & Legal approval"

Attachments uploaded: redwood_log_ttl_matrix.csv, draft_attestation.pdf (redacted sample), customer_temp_hold_form.pdf.
